posts.content_md:
Soas not to stray the original topic too far off topic I started a new thread on this.

> **Ed Wesly:** The reason that you see the scratches, etc., on your reference mirror upon replay of a transmission holo is that you made a Gabor type hologram of those features. You should be seeing "conjugate twins" of the defects when looking back at the source.

Displaced by double the angle of the reference beam. In other words, pretty far apart? Yes, absolutely. Especially if the plate is rotated 180 degrees, I see the "second" reference beam mirror come into view.

I think that's one of the things that have always fascinated me with holography as a holographer, not just an observer. Looking into my first transmission hologram made with the long coherence of the SP. I can actually look in it and see exactly where each and every component on the table was. I have one master made way back when. It was a two channel rainbow with two object beams. If I get close enough to the holo and look into it, I can see where each and every optic is. Mostly just shadows or blockers but definitely the reference mirror, the blockers to both sides, the object....it's just eerie. This is what prompted my statement a couple of years ago on how I believed a hologram not only recorded the wave front of an object but actually a slice of time in 3-D.

posts.author: jeff-blyth
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** Hummm, a harmonic coherence. Does that exist? If so can it be calculated and used?

Yes it certainly can. About 25 years ago on a ~10ft long table I once needed to make a real image 2 beam reflection H of a small model railway engine so that the image would finish up postage stamp size for a pop group's record label. I think that meant a size reduction by a factor of 2. I had a large high quality lens but its focal length was about the same as the HeNe's coherence length (~14inch) which meant that a same size real image was produced about 28 inches away and reduced size still further away. The fortunate fact is that the coherent region keeps recurring at multiples along the table (and back if reflected from a mirror). But unlike a "harmonic effect" it does not seem to diminish or become drastically less efficient over distance . So I had about a 10 inch reference beam length and several feet of object beam length from a 14-inch-only coherence length laser(ie only 7 inch depth when used on a standard Denisyuk single beam system.)

Jeff
